language-modes.note: global-settings.js renders an independently reachable language-mode control on every page, persists English, playful Hong Kong-style Cantonese, or bilingual selection in the canonical state, and synchronizes the older page projection through ding-global-settings-change. The hand-written copy inventory covers the repaired panel and metadata paths, while the overall surface remains partial until every visible and accessible string is independently localized. School mode forces English and suppresses optional controls live.

funny-levels.note: global-settings.js supplies independent English and Cantonese sliders from 1 through 5, both defaulting to 5, persists them in the canonical versioned state, and projects them to the older page runtime without lossy numeric remapping. The feature remains partial until every visible title, body, placeholder, accessible name, status, history row, and narration source uses the independent final-boundary helper.

dialog-emojis.note: global-settings.js provides a persisted Show emojis in dialogs and message boxes switch on every page. It decorates toast headings only, preserving plain control labels and accessible names.

school-mode.note: global-settings.js provides a live visitor-local School mode equivalent on every page, with rename, unlock-code digest, reset, English suppression of optional controls, and storage-clear recovery wording. The mode is explicitly described as a user-experience preference rather than a security boundary.

narration.note: global-settings.js implements an off-by-default browser narrator with late installed-voice enumeration, stable voiceURI persistence, English/Cantonese/Both serialization, rate and pitch controls, and a superseding queue. It reports browser capability honestly and never invents a voice.

scheduled-settings.note: global-settings.js provides a partial versioned bounded visitor-local rule list with target/value, date/time, weekdays or Every day, timezone-aware matching, cross-midnight handling, precedence, apply/remove, a complete effective tuple, boundary timer, visibility refresh, and separate base/effective values. Canonical theme and density state consume document root data attributes. The regex overlay remains bounded by panel geometry and source responses remain byte limited. External values never silently become permanent base settings.

external-settings-sources.note: The page equivalent in global-settings.js accepts local, validated HTTPS, loopback development, or Home Assistant endpoint choices. It rejects credentials, query strings, fragments, unsafe hosts, private production hosts, redirects, oversized or deeply nested responses, and unknown fields. Home Assistant accepts only on or off state shapes and applies effective values without writing remote values into the permanent base record. The browser credential-vault limitation is explicit.

dim-sum-surprise.note: global-settings.js consumes the versioned dim-sum-cache.json records, including authoritative bilingual names, immutable catalog-v1 release tags, exact host/repository/path/filename identity, public image URLs, and SHA-256 values. It performs a fresh ten-percent later-visit draw, one draw per launch, with first-visit, School, quiet, error, update, active-work, hidden-page, and screen-reader suppression. The rendered card uses a verified locally cached sanctioned catalog image and accessible bilingual alt text, with no CSS substitute or opt-out. First use remains partial because it requires a bounded network fetch to populate the local image cache, and the candidate set is bounded and shuffled rather than fixed to one record.

regex-builder.note: site/app.js implements a real anchored regex builder: openRegex()/initRegex() (lines 808, 812) open a <dialog> attached to the triggering field (regex-target-label shows "Attached to: <field>"), support literal-insert buttons, i/m/u flags, and previewRegex() live matching, with applyRegex() writing the result back into the originating search field. Wired from every .regex-trigger button via initSearch() (line 807), including the settings search and documentation search.

non-blocking-notifications.note: site/app.js implements notify()/notification history (renderNotifications, notification-history dialog) with bulk select/dismiss (initNotificationBulk, planBulk with destructive flag), a notification-open dialog, and export of notification history (notificationExportRows). Wired end to end from init() (line 1055).

status-hub.note: site/status.html exists as a page shell but no live status-hub project, session card, or question-card logic was found in site/app.js.

material-appearance.note: site/app.js implements a genuine infinite-colour-picker/translator (rgbToHsl/hsvToRgb/rgbToLab/rgbToOklab/hwbToRgb/cmykToRgb and translateColour, wired via initColourTranslator) plus theme/density/accent/font-scale controls in initSettings() with a live preview (initSettingsPreview). This covers colour translation and basic tokens well, but there is no per-element "Edit appearance..." editor, no Word-depth typography controls, and no named-preset export/import beyond the general settings export.

app-logo-customization.note: site/app.js wires logo-file/logo-clear to loadLogo()/applyLogo() with a logo-status readout, storing the custom logo in localStorage. This is a real local-only upload and clear path, but there is no crop/fit/background editor, no multi-size generation, and no shipped preset gallery beyond the single custom-upload slot.

local-file-converter.note: The site's many to*() functions (toJson, toXml, toYaml, toSql, toToml, toDelimited, toMarkdown, toHtml) convert the documentation/notification export data into different text formats - this is export formatting (complete-exports), not a general-purpose local file converter with a category catalogue and bundled adapters. No such converter surface exists.

ollama-suite-manager.note: No Ollama integration of any kind exists in the site.

browser-style-tabs.note: The site is a small multi-page static site (index/product/documentation/downloads/settings/status.html navigated as separate pages); no in-page browser-style tab strip, docking, or tab groups were found in site/app.js.

tab-groups-and-searches.note: No tabs exist on the site at all (see browser-style-tabs), so there are no tab groups or tab searches.

command-palette.note: site/app.js registers Ctrl+Shift+F before the navigation element early return, and global-settings.js creates complete palette markup, renames School-mode entries from the chosen name, activates the owning tab before focus, and exposes exact global-setting controls for generated articles. The surface remains partial because the broader all-feature palette inventory is not yet complete.

destructive-action-confirmation.note: site/app.js planBulk() and bulk actions carry a destructive flag (line 299, 309) that changes copy to state "This cannot be undone," and settings-reset is styled as a danger-button, but no two-key-plus-slider super-confirmation gate (the documented contract's specific mechanism) was found - only a plain destructive-labelled action.

local-version-history.note: The documentation catalogue lists a "History" article (app/history, describing append-only local configuration revisions) as PRODUCT documentation content, but no actual history/versions panel, diff view, or restore action exists in the site itself - this is a described feature of the console product, not an implemented feature of the site.

changelog-viewer.note: No changelog viewer, date filter, or commit-link rendering was found in site/app.js.

external-editor-handoff.note: No open-in-external-editor / VS Code handoff exists on the site.

complete-exports.note: site/app.js implements a genuinely broad export pipeline: toJson/toJsonl/toYaml/toToml/toXml/toSql/toDelimited/toMarkdown/toHtml plus suitableFormats()/exportFilename()/download(), used by both initDocumentationExport() and the settings/notification export paths, with an explicit personalVocabulary:"omitted" marker in the settings export payload (line ~895) matching the export-honesty contract.

bulk-actions.note: site/app.js implements planBulk()/summariseBulk()/bulkClick()/bulkSelectAll() with a reviewable affected/skipped preview and a destructive flag, wired into notification bulk-select/dismiss (initNotificationBulk).

accessibility.note: site/app.js implements a real WCAG contrast calculator (contrastRatio/contrastVerdict) used by the colour translator, and sr-only labels appear in settings.html, but no site-wide audit of focus order, ARIA roles, or reduced-motion coverage beyond the one reduceMotion() check in the counter animation (line 967) was verified.

responsive-sizing.note: site/styles.css was not inspected for a systematic responsive strategy in this pass; no JS-level narrow-width handling (comparable to the app's "narrow" screen flag) was found in site/app.js.

personal-vocabulary-upload.note: site/app.js wires vocabulary-file/vocabulary-clear to loadVocabulary()/applyVocabulary(), with bounded validation of replacement entries (from/to length limits, line ~924) and a vocabulary-status readout, storing the cache in localStorage under ding-pbx-vocabulary-cache.

per-element-toy-locks.note: No per-element lock/unlock mechanism was found anywhere in site/app.js.

support-tickets.note: No Support Tickets surface exists on the site.

unlock-ladder.note: No unlock ladder (dim sum / sums / whack-a-mole / clock) exists; there is nothing to unlock in the first place (see per-element-toy-locks).

built-in-authenticator.note: No TOTP/authenticator surface, QR generation, or code display exists in site/app.js.

attention-modes.note: site/app.js implements real ADHD/attention accommodations wired in initSettings(): reduceFlashing, simplifiedLanguage, extendedTimeouts, focus, timeAwareness, oneThing (with updateOneThingBanner and a current-task field), and momentum (initMomentum/checkMomentum/updateSessionTimer), all persisted through state.attention and off by default per DEFAULTS.

browser-extension-download-surfaces.note: This is a static documentation/marketing site; there is no browser extension and no Start-download/Downloading/complete dialog surfaces.

offline-documentation-browser.note: site/documentation.html plus renderDestinations()/initDocumentationExport() in site/app.js present a searchable documentation catalogue with per-article export, but this is a static site consuming its own bundled catalogue over the network at page load, not an offline-bundled in-app documentation browser matching the console-app contract.

app-display-name.note: global-settings.js exposes a renameable visitor-local display name on every page, updates the document title, brand labels, data-display-name labels, and body consumer inventory, and provides a super-confirmed reset action. An explicit identity boundary keeps shipped package identity, data directory, installer identity, and update feed fixed.

guided-forms.note: No guided/picker-driven form beyond ordinary settings selects and file inputs was found; there is no enumerated-picker-over-freeform-text pattern comparable to the app's endpoint wizard.

bounded-overlays.note: The regex builder (openRegex) and command palette (openPalette) both use native <dialog>.showModal(), which the browser bounds to the viewport and paints its own surface, and openRegex() explicitly labels which field it is attached to ("Attached to: <field>"). This satisfies the bounded/anchored-overlay contract for these two surfaces.

context-menu-shortcuts.note: No context menu (oncontextmenu handling) exists anywhere on the site.

long-operation-progress.note: The only progress-shaped code found is a decorative counter-animation easing function (line 967), not a real operation-progress report inside a start dialog.

in-context-recovery.note: No surface-level recovery route (for example re-authentication offered directly beside a refused action) was found.

provider-markup-rendering.note: No renderer for remote/provider-authored Markdown or rich text was found; documentation content in renderDestinations() is inserted as plain escaped text/HTML built by the site itself, not rendered from provider-authored markup.

forge-publishing.note: No GitHub/forge publishing flow exists; this is a documentation/marketing site with no repository-publishing feature.

collapsible-filters.note: site/settings.html and site/documentation.html use real <details class="collapsible-panel"> elements wrapping the search/filter controls (settings-filters-panel, documentation-filters-panel), wired to updateFilterStatus() in site/app.js which reports match counts into an aria-live status span - a genuine collapsible, accessible filter row.

automatic-updates.note: The static-page equivalent in global-settings.js reports the truthful local state that no verified release manifest or installer is published for this page. It intentionally exposes no refresh or download control until a manifest can drive a real action, so there is no inert update affordance.
